asignatura: INICIACIÓN A HABILIDADES COMUNICATIVAS EN INGLÉS(B)
resumen:
Public speaking is crucial, professionally relevant and can be learnt (slide 2).
Reasons: boost self-esteem, confidence, assertiveness, leadership, writing skills, think on your feet (p. 6; slide 3).
Hot tips: focus on the message, believe it, prepare, breathe and move, don't memorise, eye contact, have fun (p. 8-9).
Eye contact may be one of the most difficult aspects of giving a presentation (p. 10).
Presentations are planned with a chart: aim, topic, outline, timing, visual aids, audience's attention (p. 11; slide 6).

tarjetas.pregunta: Name three reasons for public speaking.
tarjetas.respuesta: Self-esteem, confidence, assertiveness, leadership, thinking on your feet (p. 6).

tarjetas.pregunta: Why shouldn't you memorise your speech?
tarjetas.respuesta: It puts too much pressure on you; if you go blank you won't know what to do (p. 8).

tarjetas.pregunta: What to have instead of a memorised speech?
tarjetas.respuesta: A short punchy opening and a few points as memory joggers (p. 8).
Your brain works better, it dissipates nervous energy and connects with the audience (p. 8).

tarjetas.pregunta: Who should you make eye contact with first?
tarjetas.respuesta: Someone at the back of the room, so your voice carries (p. 8).
For many it is an intimate act, almost like touching someone (p. 10).
Aim, topic, outline, timing, visual aids, audience's attention (slide 6).

tarjetas.pregunta: Should you worry about grammar when speaking?
tarjetas.respuesta: No; speak normally and from the heart (p. 8).
